shared_elements: low-relief carving on pale stone slab
a row of repeated arch-like or fringed motifs across the upper zone
bird-like forms with beak and eye
rounded/arched upper edge of the slab
weathered breaks and losses along the surface
justification: Both are shallow relief carvings on pale stone with a rounded top, organised into stacked horizontal zones and topped by a row of repeated arch- or fringe-like motifs, with profile creatures below — the closest specific correspondence being that upper repeated-arch band over a hatched/linear border. Beyond that they diverge sharply: A is a thick free-standing pillar with schematic, isolated animals floating on blank ground, while B is a thin flat stela crowded with detailed clothed human figures, offering stands and hieroglyph-like signs in a coherent narrative scene.
